correctness.rationale: Dyck up-step sets are the bases of Catalan matroid. A shattered support S is exactly independently extendable for both all-up and all-down assignments; matroid basis exchange fills in intermediate traces. Since first position is up and last down, only internal paired Q_i={2i,2i+1} can occur. Prefix constraints yield for N=n−1, d=N−|S| the exact strip path h_0=0, h_i=h_{i−1}+1−|S∩Q_i|, 0≤h_i≤d and h_N=d. Choices per pair give tridiagonal transfer A_d with diag2, offdiag1, so coefficient [z^k]Φ_n=(A_{N-k}^N)_{0,N-k}. Top coefficients 2^N and (3^N−1)/2 are exact; an explicit support with a doubly selected pair is maximal of size n−2 for n≥4, establishing nonpurity. Independent exhaustive raw Dyck traces match all coefficients for n=1..6.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration is a corroboration; unbounded n proof uses matroid exchange and exact transfer matrix.

originality.rationale: Ardila proves Dyck up-position sets form Catalan-matroid bases; this foundational equivalence and matroid exchange are not novel. Engström–Sanyal–Stump define a lexicographic standard complex of lattice-path matroids, not this ordinary coordinate shattering complex: n=4 gives 14 Catalan bases versus 28 shattered supports. The nontrivial bounded-strip weighted-walk enumeration gives the full ordinary trace/shattering polynomial and explicit nonpurity witness, which are not implied by those inspected primary statements.
residual_risks: Catalan matroid basis description and matroid all-positive/all-negative trace criterion are classical and not novel.
Engström–Sanyal–Stump standard complexes count different faces; an equivalent ordinary trace enumeration under alternative matroid terminology remains possible.
Complete classification of all inclusion-maximal shattered supports is not claimed, only nonpurity witness and full f-polynomial.
